title: Customer Trajectory Scorecard — QBR-ready template
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working QBR-ready scorecard template for Customer Success Managers to rapidly assess account trajectory ahead of renewal conversations. Focus: combine adoption signals + risk flags into a single interpretable number and a short playbook for action. Use during QBR prep, weekly account reviews, and renewal forecasting cycles.

High-level approach (draft):
- Multi-dimensional scoring: Usage, Feature Adoption, Business Impact (value capture), Financial / Contract health, Support & SLAs, and Relationship / Strategic fit.
- Each dimension has 3–6 signals (raw telemetry + qualitative inputs).
- Signals are normalized to 0–100, dimension scores are weighted, then summed to final index (0–100).
- Quick triage categories: Green >= 75, Yellow 50–74, Red < 50.

Scoring matrix (example weights — tune per cohort):
- Usage (30%): DAU/MAU for product modules relevant to paid seats (weight: 0.30)
- Adoption (20%): % of key features used weekly (weight: 0.20)
- Business Impact (20%): Number of workflows automated or revenue influenced, exec-level references (weight: 0.20)
- Support & Reliability (10%): P0 incidents, time-to-resolution, escalations (weight: 0.10)
- Financial/Commercial (10%): On-contract spend, payment status, expansion/downsizing signals (weight: 0.10)
- Relationship & Exec Sponsorship (10%): CSM sentiment, named sponsor level, advocacy (weight: 0.10)

Signals and quick normalization rules (working list):
- Usage: Monthly active seats / committed seats => normalized = min(100, (MAU/committed_seats)*100).
- Session length: compare 90-day median to product baseline. If >= baseline -> 100, else scale down linearly to 0.
- Feature breadth: (# key features used weekly / total key features) * 100.
- Feature depth: % of power users performing advanced workflows (90th percentile usage).
- Value signal: number of workflows moved off legacy systems * 20 (cap at 100).
- Support load: tickets per 100 seats -> map to 100->0 scale (example: 0–2 tickets=100, 3–5=60, >5=20).
- SLA breaches: each breach subtracts 15 points (floor 0).
- Payment timeliness: current = 100, 1 late=60, >1 late or disputes=10.
- Renewal intent (qual): mapped from Net Promoter/CSAT/meeting notes: promoter=100, neutral=60, detractor=10.

Computing overall score (simple formula):
- For each dimension: dimension_score = average(normalized_signals_for_dimension)
- Overall_score = SUM_i (dimension_score_i * weight_i) // result 0–100
- Flagging: if any critical signal (P0 incidents in 30d, major SLA breach, exec sponsor resigned) -> automatic YELLOW/RED override depending on severity.

Quick worksheet header (copy into sheet):
- account_name | account_owner | renewal_date | committed_seats | current_spend | overall_score | color | usage_score | adoption_score | impact_score | support_score | financial_score | relationship_score | top_risks | next_actions | action_owner | eta

Sample scoring vignette (fictional):
- Acme Retail: committed 100 seats, MAU for paid seats 92 -> usage_score ~92. Key features used weekly 3/6 -> adoption_score ~50. Product automated 2 workflows (value=40). Support: 1 ticket/100 seats -> 100. Payment on time -> 100. Exec sponsor engaged -> 100. Applying weights -> overall ~ (92*0.3)+(50*0.2)+(40*0.2)+(100*0.1)+(100*0.1)+(100*0.1)=81 -> GREEN.

Risk flags (operationalized):
- Red flags (immediate outreach & escalation):
  - Exec sponsor resigned or reduced scope.
  - 2+ P0 incidents in last 30 days.
  - Multiple overdue invoices or active billing dispute.
  - Usage < 30% of committed seats for two consecutive months.
- Yellow flags (monitor + playbook):
  - Feature adoption stagnation (no growth in key feature users in 60d).
  - Increased support volume (3–5 tickets/100 seats).
  - Negative NPS feedback from 2+ stakeholders.

Suggested playbooks (actionable templates):
- Red — "Save-the-renewal":
  - Owner: AE + CSM + Solutions Eng (SE) sync within 48 hours.
  - Steps: 1) Exec alignment call w/ new sponsor; 2) Triage incidents + mitigation plan; 3) Offer short-term incentives (discount, pilot credits) tied to a 90d remediation plan; 4) Escalate to success leader if no sponsor or unresolved billing.
- Yellow — "Adoption Sprint":
  - Owner: CSM + Product Educator.
  - Steps: 1) 4-week focused enablement (2 workshops + targeted playbooks); 2) Create 3 success metrics mapped to workflows; 3) Weekly progress emails and short demo check-ins; 4) If no improvement after 6 weeks -> escalate to AE for commercial levers.

QBR section skeleton (keep short):
- "Where we are" — current score, key movements since last QBR, top 3 wins.
- "Value realized" — qualitative + quantitative (savings, time saved, revenue influenced).
- "Risks & mitigation" — top risks from scorecard + action plan owners and ETA.
- "Next 90d plan" — adoption goals, success milestones, enablement calendar, executive check-ins.

Operational notes and rollout checklist (for CS leaders):
- Pilot with 10 accounts across SMB, Midmarket, and Enterprise cohorts for 8 weeks.
- Collect feedback: are weights representative? Do signals correlate with renewals?
- Add telemetry hooks: ensure CSMs can see raw signals in console and edit qualitative inputs.
- Build a one-click export from account page to QBR slide deck.

Notes to self / open questions (work-in-progress):
- Do we want different weight tables per cohort (enterprise vs. SMB)? Likely yes — add cohort-specific template.
- Should we incorporate usage velocity (week-over-week change) rather than absolute? Might catch fast-degrading accounts earlier.
- How to best normalize cross-product usage for multi-product customers.

References and next artifacts to produce:
- dashboard spec for scorecard metrics (owner: Ivy Chen)
- rollout comms + CSM playbook (owner: Liam O'Rourke)
- evaluation plan to compare historical renewal outcomes (JIRA-7321)

If using: copy header into a Google Sheet and populate with last 6 months of data before QBR prep. Keep comments short in the sheet cell (1–2 lines) so slides are export-friendly.

End of template — please comment with missing signals or edge cases.
